name: Shelf sea
notes: Open continental-shelf water: no land plants; the shoreline where the shelf sea meets the coast carries eelgrass, saltmarsh cordgrass and strandline weed, and the seabed carries seagrass and brown algae in the photic zone. Drawn on North Sea/Baltic, NW Atlantic (Georges Bank), and Australian shelf; underwater species flagged.

ground.name: Eelgrass
ground.origin: North Atlantic and North Pacific coasts
ground.source: underwater — Zostera marina, N Hemisphere shelf shallows on sand, temperate seagrass meadows 0.3-1.2 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: underwater — Zostera marina, N Hemisphere shelf shallows on sand, temperate seagrass meadows 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: submerged; leaves sheathed on a creeping rhizome

ground.silhouette: submerged meadow of long green ribbons streaming with tide

growth.juvenile_note: The seed splits and a white seedling axis anchors in sandy mud; a green cotyledon is followed by 2-3 narrow, flat, bright green ribbon leaves from a sheath. The seedling soon grows a creeping white rhizome with roots at each node and new shoots along it, so a first-year plant is a short row of leafy tufts; leaf length (a few cm to over 1 m) depends on water depth and clarity.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Zostera marina): leaves to 1.2 cm wide and over 1 m long (a few cm in clear shallow water), perennial but may grow as an annual, several thousand seeds per m2, inflorescence about 10 cm, one meadow clone about 3000 years old. Germination, seedling growth, flowering age and shoot life estimated from eelgrass restoration studies.

ground.name: Smooth cordgrass
ground.source: Sporobolus alterniflorus, sheltered shelf-sea shorelines of the NW Atlantic, low-marsh cordgrass 0.5-2 m — Wikipedia

traits.native_range: Sporobolus alterniflorus, sheltered shelf-sea shorelines of the NW Atlantic, low-marsh cordgrass 0
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.note: smooth hollow green culms with pale nodes; the whole shoot turns straw and dies in autumn

ground.silhouette: tall smooth cordgrass belt fringing the channel edge

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: one soft shoot with flat, tapering, bright-green leaves; it tillers within weeks and sends out rhizomes, reaching ~15 cm in 3-4 months. The same species as Spartina alterniflora (current name). Each culm lives about a year, but the rhizome clone spreads up to 3 m a season and persists for decades.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Spartina alterniflora (germinates Apr-Jun, flowers Jun-Oct, 0.4-2.5 m, shoots die back in autumn); USDA NRCS Cape May PMC Plant Guide (most seed germinates in 7-10 d after 1-4 months cold-wet storage; ~15 cm in 3-4 months; 2.5-3 m lateral spread per season; cover in 2-3 seasons)
